pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

✨Let’s make a  to go mug from clay ✨ I have been wanting to make a to go cup for a while. And I’m excited that I finally have done it. I actually made quite a few of them. And before I could take any pictures, they completely sold out at my last market. Lesson learned, always take your pictures! But that’s OK just give me excuse to make more.  when you’re joining pieces of clay, it’s best practice to pieces with the same moisture level to prevent cracking. But I do think I am going to let these set up a little bit more in the future. This is because it was a little difficult to get that lip, perfectly parallel to the rim of the cup.   I did end up managing to get it done perfectly, but it took a lot of time  (and patience 😅). using a heat gun is probably one of the more life-saving tools for a potter, especially when handbilling from clay. But keep in mind it’s also easy to burn yourself since you can’t see an actual flame the way you do with the torch. Safety first!  Hope you enjoyed this video and be sure to tag me in your to go cups! ✨🤗🤍 #ceramics  #pottery  #howtomakepottery #howtomakeamug #potters #artist #ceramist  #ceramicpottery

In this Tips video I go over how I cut my pieces off of the hump. I’ve seen quite a few different techniques from various potters on this process, but I’ve found this to be what works for me. I can’t stress enough practicing the technique before committing to trying to make pots to alleviate a lot of the frustration that can come from figuring it out. I think a lot of people give up on it because of this and as we all know, persistence pays off in ceramics. I hope this video helps and I’ll keep making them…If anybody’s interested in learning more about these techniques I do have a workshop coming up in January at Jewell Town Pottery in Massachusetts.
